questions.text: Who compares the packing slip with the Excel order?
Who manually counts and checks the goods?
Who determines whether the received quantity differs from the order?
Who visually checks whether packaging or goods are damaged?
Who accepts the actual received quantity?
Who emails the supplier about the quantity difference?
Who sends the supplier credit claim?
Who checks whether the same item is already present?
Who moves the older and newer batches into position?
After the credit claim, are damaged goods held, stored, returned or handled another way?
What is the relative timing of quantity checks, visual checks, storage and accountant entries? These topics are described separately; their displayed relative order needs confirmation.
For Supplier 1, when and where are item, batch, quantity and best-before date recorded, and by whom?
Which ERP transactions does the accountant make for Supplier 1, and are they made after receipt or after order completion?

notes: Reviewable draft, not human-approved. Scope and the existing damaged-goods clarification boundary are retained.

Scope: Supplier 1 receipt, inspection, stock placement and accountant ERP follow-up. Other suppliers and own production are excluded. The advance Excel order is an input; upstream stock review and order preparation remain outside the retained view.

Supplier 1 checks include goods, batch, best-before date and quantity. General receipt practice includes manual counting, paper-document checks, visual inspection and recording item, batch, quantity and best-before date. Recording details need clarification.

The source states document comparison, checks and then storage for Supplier 1. Quantity-difference handling and quality control are described separately. Their precise relative timing remains unresolved; displayed ordering is for review, not a confirmed operational sequence.
Storage is a stated common continuation. Matching quantities and absence of an existing batch bypass only the corresponding conditional actions; no additional actions are inferred.
After a damage credit claim, physical disposition and continuation are unspecified. The unmapped boundary does not assert that the actual process ends there.

Accountants perform necessary ERP transactions after receipt or order completion; warehouse workers do not perform ERP transactions. The purchase-invoice entry specified for other suppliers is not attributed to Supplier 1.
Warehouse locations are established and arranged by handling speed across Warehouse 1 and Warehouse 2. Rare cross-docking and packaging accounting remain outside this retained view.

Future needs, excluded from current-process nodes: ERP purchase orders and visibility of ordered goods, electronic receipt and inspection against ERP orders, and more automated packaging-tax calculations.
source:
Example 1
Company: Põllukuld AS
Field of activity: Food industry
Sample: The process of receiving and storing goods
Note: "Need" refers to the future need identified in the workshop and is not part of today's process.
1. Receipt of goods
Today's process
When making purchase orders, the current stock of the goods is viewed.
For Supplier 1: 
the order is prepared in advance in Excel;
upon the arrival of the goods, the driver gives the warehouse a paper packing slip;
the packing slip is compared with the order created in Excel;
in the warehouse, the goods, batch, best before date and quantity are checked;
then the goods are stored;
If the same item is present, the older batch is moved forward and the new batch is placed backwards.
In the case of goods arriving from other suppliers, there is no pre-created order in Excel: 
the goods are inspected on the basis of the delivery note;
the goods received, batch, best before and quantity are marked on the consignment note;
the delivery note is forwarded to the accountant;
the accountant enters the information into the ERP as a purchase invoice.
Goods arriving at the warehouse from our own production are not inspected upon receipt.
Need: It  must be possible to see the goods that have already been ordered in the ERP. For this, you want to start using purchase orders.
2. Identification and inspection of the goods
Today's process
The goods are counted and checked manually on the basis of paper documents.
If there is an order in Excel, it will be compared with the packing slip or delivery note provided by the driver.
Need: In the future, the receipt and inspection of goods will be carried out electronically and the received goods will be compared with the previously prepared order in the system.
3. Handling of differences
Today's process
If the goods arrive more or less than ordered, the actual quantity will be accepted.
The supplier will be informed of the difference by e-mail.
4. Data recorded at the appointment
Upon receipt of the goods, the following shall be recorded:
merchandise;
batch;
quantity;
Best before date.
5. Quality Control
Today's process
Upon receipt of goods, it is visually checked whether the goods are intact.
If the packaging is broken or the item is otherwise damaged, a credit claim will be sent to the supplier.
6. Making ERP entries
Today's process
Warehouse workers do not make ERP transactions themselves.
After the goods have been received or the order has been completed, the necessary ERP transactions are made by the accountant.
7. Storage of goods
Today's process
Goods have established specific locations in the warehouse.
Goods are arranged according to their handling speed, i.e. how quickly they move through the warehouse.
The warehouse has two floors: Warehouse 1 and Warehouse 2.
For different batches of the same item, the older batch is placed forward and the newer batch is placed backward.
8. Cross-docking
Today's process
Forwarding of received goods directly to dispatch without intermediate storage is very rare.
9. Packaging accounting
Today's process
Historically, the packaging accompanying goods arriving from outside Estonia has been overweighed.
Based on the received quantities, the taxable portion related to packaging is calculated in Excel.
Need: ERP must enable the calculation of the taxable portion related to packaging more automatically than before.
10. Source documents for receipt of goods
Today, the following documents are used for the receipt of goods:
Delivery note;
packing slip;
An order created in Excel.
Summary of identified needs
Three main future needs were identified in the workshop:
Implementation of purchase orders in ERP
The ordered goods must be visible in the ERP even before the physical arrival of the goods.
Electronic Goods Receipt and Control
It must be possible to check the received goods electronically against the purchase order in the ERP.
Automation of packaging accounting
The ERP must support a more automated calculation of the taxable portion related to packaging.
